instructions.intake.pointer: agent-governance-suite intake guide: skip rereading only while the current context retains both evidence of a successful read of the common intake and selection criteria in {path} and that text. Otherwise, including after either is lost to compaction, read that section before task work and follow it. Failed reads, partial output, or another revision do not count as a successful read.
instructions.intake.skills:
Skills are split by purpose. For every user message, before answering or using the next tool, match the judgment or action that message calls for against each skill's targets below, and call every matching skill now, before that judgment or action (questions and check requests included). Choose by whether the judgment you will actually make falls under the targets, not by names or keywords. A skill called earlier applies only to the judgment or action it was called for; do not apply an earlier skill's guidance that does not fit this purpose. When some work can be completed and verified on its own, consider delegating it to a subagent before doing it yourself. When delegating, write the goal, scope, forbidden areas, write ownership, the chosen skills and the completion and verification criteria in the brief, and do not hand off waiting such as watching a build or polling progress.

instructions.sessionMessage.guide: To send a session message, fix the target, body and TTL with prepare_session_message, receive the system-issued messageId, then send it with send_session_message(messageId). Do not make up an ID yourself or put the content into send again. If the send result is unclear, query status or retry send with the same ID you received. An unknown ID may mean that an earlier send completed or that its records were cleaned up, so compare it with the saved receipt. Use a new prepare only for a new send intent, and do not unconditionally prepare an unclear earlier send again. A successful send means the message was queued, not that the recipient received or processed it. If autoWake.state is available after send, do not wake the recipient separately with a host feature. If it is no-live-relay or unsupported, the AGS automatic wake path is unavailable, so wake the recipient once with a host feature only when its processing is needed now. If it is no-live-relay or unsupported and the recipient's processing is needed now, tell the user the confirmed delivery state and the fact that the AGS automatic wake path is unavailable. wake-unanswered under available is the fact that a handed-off wake has no evidence of an answer yet; it may ring again once its resend time has passed. degraded means that this recipient session's automatic wake has failed repeatedly or lacks a prerequisite; the message stays queued and may be delayed until the recipient takes it over at its own turn end, tool boundary or input. If it is degraded and the recipient's processing is needed now, tell the user the confirmed delivery state and the fact that the message may be delayed until the recipient takes it over at a boundary. autoWake is an advisory automatic-wake value as of its basis time (authorityEffect: none); it is not evidence of the recipient's current work or sleep state, or of message delivery, processing or approval. In a report that is needed, use only the confirmed queueing and delivery state, and do not conclude from autoWake alone that the recipient is awake now or that delivery will follow. After a normal send, do not repeat a receipt or status query or a receipt-confirmation report for each message. The recipient collects only the messageIds it actually processed and ACKs them at once with acknowledge_session_messages. It does not ACK IDs it could not process, which keeps their redelivery possible. An ACK confirms that a message was processed; it is not evidence of task completion or approval. Even when you receive a wake signal without a body or a message without content, do not stop the work in progress, and do not guess the content of a message whose body you did not receive. Send a message only when there is a new result, a blocker or a decision request, once, to the one recipient that needs it; do not create reports about reports, resends of the same content, relays only for relaying, or round-trip messages only to confirm receipt.
